title: Connections, overload and capacity
brief: Budget admitted work and recovery headroom around the resource that actually limits the service.
outcomes: Distinguish connections, active work and queued requests
Choose bounded overload behaviour and capacity evidence
entry: Application pools and basic transaction boundaries; deeper query, lock and version mechanisms are preparation for the capacity branch that uses them.

neighbours.RL103: Owns initial triage and investigation before selecting a capacity branch.
neighbours.RL87: Supplies execution-work reasoning before query-specific capacity changes.
neighbours.RL91: Supplies contention reasoning for a hot-row bottleneck.
neighbours.RL92: Supplies retained-version reasoning before history/headroom changes.

heading.title: From requests to active work
heading.brief: Count all application replicas and pools; separate admission, connection waiting, server execution and response time.

heading.title: The limiting resource
heading.brief: Locally distinguish CPU, I/O, memory and one hot stock row using an illustrative load curve; show why admitting more work can lengthen queues. Prepare query-work reasoning in RL87 or lock reasoning in RL91 when that bottleneck calls for a deeper intervention; pool admission can be understood without either full branch.

heading.title: Controlled overload
heading.brief: Choose admission limits, deadlines, cancellation and retry budgets; prevent queued work and retries from prolonging recovery.

heading.title: Headroom for failure
heading.brief: Budget space and throughput for retained history, backups, rebuilds and failover; take retained-version reasoning from RL92 before changing history lifetimes. Distinguish measured capacity from a universal safe percentage.
